title: Playlist search bar reveals on scroll-to-top instead of pull-to-reveal only
claim: ISSUES.md documents ServerPlaylistDetailView's `.searchable(... placement: .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .automatic))` as broken at step 4: after scrolling down and back to the top, iOS auto-reveals the search bar regardless of how the user got there. It lists two failed remediation attempts and three 'plausible paths forward', i.e. presents the defect as unresolved.
description: The playlist screen used to pop its search field back into view on its own whenever you scrolled back to the top, instead of only when you deliberately pulled down.
issue: Nothing goes wrong for a user today. Filmed on a 60-song playlist, all five of ISSUES.md's desired steps now hold, including the one it documents as failing: scrolling back to the top leaves the search field hidden.
proposed_fix: No code change. ISSUES.md is stale — delete this section or move it to a resolved list. Ethan stated it directly: 'that issues MD document talking about the search bar being broken is not true, that has been fixed but now works as intended.' The fix taken was a placement change, closest to the document's third option: `.searchable(placement: .automatic)` plus `.searchToolbarBehavior(.automatic)` via `musicNativeSearchable`, which on iOS 26 collapses the field into a toolbar search button on scroll instead of a navigation-bar drawer.
steps: Seed a playlist long enough to scroll, inside the account's own data: Subsonic createPlaylist "T344 Scroll Probe" with 60 random songs.

Source (CORRECTED — see notes): ServerPlaylistViews.swift:979 applies `.playlistTrackSearchable(enabled: !isAlbumStyleDetail, text: $searchText)`, which calls `musicNativeSearchable` (MusicDesignSystem.swift:1003-1006) → `.searchable(text:, placement: .automatic, prompt:)` + `.searchToolbarBehavior(.automatic)`. The `.navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .automatic)` placement ISSUES.md names is gone from this view.
Drive and record: Library → Playlists → 'T344 Scroll Probe, 60 songs'; dump after each of ISSUES.md's five steps.
Step 1, open: no SearchField in the tree — hidden. (desired: hidden)
Step 2, pull down at top: SearchField {{16,117},{370×44}} label 'Search' appears. (desired: appears)
Step 3, scroll down 4 swipes: no SearchField; a toolbar Button 'Search' at {{326,798}}. (desired: hides)
Step 4, scroll back to top 4 swipes, settle 2.5 s: no SearchField — stays hidden. (desired: stays hidden — this is the step ISSUES.md says fails)
Step 5, pull down again: SearchField {{16,117},{370×44}} appears. (desired: appears)
notes: CORRECTION OF THIS RUN'S OWN EARLIER EVIDENCE. The previous session recorded this as already_fixed because 'the defective `.searchable` modifier was REMOVED from ServerPlaylistDetailView', based on a grep for the literal `.searchable` that found only AddToPlaylistSheet. That was wrong: the detail view still applies `.searchable`, through the `playlistTrackSearchable` → `musicNativeSearchable` wrapper that a literal grep cannot see. The status survives, but on different and stronger evidence — the documented step-4 behaviour now filmed working — rather than on an absent modifier. The earlier claim that 'there is no interaction left to film' was consequently also wrong, which is why this finding now carries a video instead of a null. Lesson for a full run: verify absence claims by symbol and wrapper, not by literal grep.
